diagnostic_evidence.quote: A random variable $X$ is said to follow a \emph{sub-Gaussian distribution} if there exists some $K > 0$, such that $\mathbbm{E} \exp(X^2/K^2) \leq 2.$

issues.failure_explanation: The formula $\inf_{t>0}\E\exp(X^2/t^2)$ equals 1 for every random variable (attained as $t\to\infty$), so the definition assigns $\|X\|_{\psi_2}=1$ universally. The intended sub-Gaussian norm is $\inf\{t>0 : \E\exp(X^2/t^2)\leq 2\}$, consistent with the preceding correct characterization via $\E\exp(X^2/K^2)\leq 2$.

failure_location.quote: the sub-Gaussian norm of $X$, denoted by $\|X\|_{\psi_2}$ is defined to be, $$ \|X\|_{\psi_2} = \underset{t>0}{\inf} \ \E \exp(X^2/t^2).$$

issues.overall_effect: The displayed formula defines the wrong quantity. Results use the correct concept of sub-Gaussian distributions and treat $\|X\|_{\psi_2}$ as a parameter; no numerical results are affected.
issues.title: Sub-Gaussian norm definition is mathematically incorrect
issues.why_classification: A single local formula correction preserves all claims; the correct concept is clear from the preceding sentence and no proof or result uses the wrong formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\|\vu_{(k)} - \vv_{(k)}\| \leq \|\vu-\vv\|_\infty$ for any two vectors $\vu$ and $\vv$ and their $k$-th order statistics
Without loss of generality, we can also assume that the rows $\{\va^\vx_i\}$ and $\{\va^{\hat{\vx}}_i\}$ of $\mat{A}^\vx$ and $\mat{A}^{\hat{\vx}}$ respectively have been reordered

issues.failure_explanation: The trimmed vectors $\mat{A}^\vx\vx$ and $\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx$ are sorted by different orderings (by $|\va_i^T\vx|$ and $|\va_i^T\hat\vx|$), so their $j$-th entries can come from different rows of $\mat{A}$ and can have opposite signs. The cited order-statistics result bounds $|y|_{(j)}-|z|_{(j)}$ (sorted absolute values) but not the signed entries $y_{i_j}-z_{i'_j}$ of differently sorted vectors. The bound is false: for $\mat{A}=I_2$, $\vx=(1,-2)$, $\hat\vx=(2,-1)$, the LHS is $20$ while the RHS is $2$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the vector-difference bound with a direct trimmed-norm comparison: bound $|\|\mat{A}^\vx\vx\|^2-\|\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx\|^2|$ via the order statistics of $\{y_i^2\}$ and Cauchy–Schwarz on the trimmed sum, preserving the same $\varepsilon$ and $m$ orders.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main trimming result (uniform geometry preservation for trimmed face-splitting measurements) is invalid. The informal restatement in thm:main-informal that gives the positive trimming guarantee is also unsupported.
issues.title: False key inequality in proof of trimming TensorRIP theorem
issues.why_classification: The key inequality is false and the proof needs a nontrivial replacement argument (trimmed-norm comparison via order statistics), but the theorem statement, the net-plus-concentration proof architecture, and the sample-complexity order all survive with a contained fix.

issues.failure_explanation: $\Theta_k$ is defined as the $m_{\text{trim}}$ indices with smallest residuals, giving $|\Theta_k|=m_{\text{trim}}$. But the trimmed matrix $\mat{A}_k=\sqrt{m/(m-m_{\text{trim}})}\mat{A}[\Theta_k,:]$ and Definition def:trimmed-matrix both require keeping $m-m_{\text{trim}}$ rows (all rows except the $m_{\text{trim}}$ with largest residuals). The gradient-step scaling $m/|\Theta_k|=m/m_{\text{trim}}$ is inconsistent with the implied scaling $m/(m-m_{\text{trim}})$ of the rescaled matrix, confirming the row-set size is wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change $\Theta_k=\left[i_1,\ldots,i_{m-m_{\text{trim}}}\right]$ to keep the $m-m_{\text{trim}}$ rows with smallest residuals.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm as written uses only $m_{\text{trim}}$ rows (a small subsample with large weights) instead of $m-m_{\text{trim}}$ rows (outlier-trimmed measurements), so it does not implement the trimmed gradient step whose convergence is analyzed in thm:main_path and whose geometry-preservation is established in theorem:trim_trip.
issues.title: TrimTIHT keeps wrong row set in gradient step
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol change in the subscript of $\Theta_k$ restores consistency with the trimmed-matrix definition, the rescaling formula, and the convergence analysis; the algorithm, its guarantees, and its scope all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let all quantities be as defined in the statement of \cref{thm:main_path}, in particular, $\mat{A} \vx^* =\vb$.

issues.failure_explanation: $\mat{A}_t\in\R^{(m-k)\times n^d}$ and $\vb=\mathcal{A}(\tX^*)\in\R^m$, so $\mat{A}_t\vz-\vb$ subtracts vectors of different dimensions and $f$ is undefined. The intended function is $f(\vz)=\|\mat{A}_t(\vz-\vx^*)\|^2/2$, whose gradient $\nabla f(\vz)=\mat{A}_t^T\mat{A}_t(\vz-\vx^*)$ is the one used in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\vb$ with $\mat{A}_t\vx^*$ in the definition of $f$.
issues.overall_effect: The function $f$ is not well-defined as stated. The proof computes with the correct gradient of the intended function, so the lemma's conclusion holds after repairing the definition; Lemma lem:rho_dist and Theorem thm:main_path are unaffected.
issues.title: Ill-defined function in Lemma strong_convexity
issues.why_classification: A single symbol change restores the definition; the proof and all downstream results are correct for the intended function.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement raises the per-step contraction factor (which depends on $t$ through $\mu_t,\rho_t,\Delta_t,\xi_t,\mat{A}_t$) to the power $t+1$ and multiplies by $\|\tR^0\|$. Iterating the one-step bound yields the product $\prod_{s=0}^{t}(\text{factor}_s)\cdot\|\tR^0\|$, not $(\text{factor}_t)^{t+1}\cdot\|\tR^0\|$; these differ whenever the contraction factors vary across iterations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the one-step bound $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \leq \alpha_t\|\tR^t\|_F$ and note the multi-step bound $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \leq \prod_{s=0}^{t}\alpha_s\cdot\|\tR^0\|_F$.
issues.overall_effect: The multi-step convergence bound in the theorem statement is incorrect. The one-step contraction rate (the substantive content of the proof) is established correctly and iterating it gives the correct multi-step bound.
issues.title: Wrong iteration formula in TrimTIHT convergence statement
issues.why_classification: The one-step bound is correct and its iteration is mechanical; the fix is a local formula correction that preserves the per-iteration contraction guarantee with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion $\|\tR^{k+1}\|\leq 5\delta\|\tR^k\|+c$ with $\|\tR^1\|=\|\tX^*\|$ (since $\tX_1^1=0$) yields $\|\tR^{k+1}\|\leq(5\delta)^k\|\tX^*\|+c/(1-5\delta)$ after $k$ iterations. The proof claims $(5\delta)^{k+1}$ instead of $(5\delta)^k$, overclaiming by a factor of $5\delta$. The statement also references undefined $\tR^0$ instead of the initial residual $\tR^1=-\tX^*$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the exponent from $k+1$ to $k$ and replace $\|\tR^0\|_F$ with $\|\tX^*\|_F$ (the initial residual norm).
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence rate $(5\delta)^{k+1}$ is incorrect; the correct rate is $(5\delta)^k$. The qualitative guarantee (geometric convergence with factor $5\delta$) and the noise floor are preserved.
issues.title: Off-by-one in KaczTIHT convergence exponent
issues.why_classification: A one-unit exponent correction and one reference fix preserve the geometric convergence rate, the noise guarantee, and all scope; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The intermediate step derives $\frac{1}{m}\|\mat{A}^T\bm{\eta}\|_2$ for the leading noise contribution to $\|\lambda\bm{\eta}_{err}\|$, but the final line of the bound writes $\|\mat{A}^T\bm{\eta}\|_2$ (dropping $\frac{1}{m}$). Substituting this final-line bound into the convergence recursion gives a noise term larger by a factor of $m$ than the theorem's stated formula, so the proof as written does not derive the theorem's noise guarantee.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the $\frac{1}{m}$ factor in front of $\|\mat{A}^T\bm{\eta}\|_2$ in the proof's final noise-bound line.
issues.overall_effect: The proof's noise analysis is internally inconsistent: the intermediate derivation is correct but the final simplification drops $\frac{1}{m}$ from the $\|\mat{A}^T\bm{\eta}\|_2$ term, and the theorem's conclusion uses the correct (tighter) bound that does not follow from the proof's stated intermediate step.
issues.title: Dropped 1/m factor in KaczTIHT noise bound derivation
issues.why_classification: A single factor restoration in one proof line makes the derivation consistent with the theorem's formula; the noise guarantee and all other claims are preserved.
